headline: CEO highlights constant-currency EBIT growth of 21% in FY26, masking reported profit decline driven by AUD strength
reasoning: On a reported basis, Nanosonics posted revenue of $203.9 million (up 2.7%) but net profit fell almost 14% to $17.8 million. However, Michael Kavanagh argues the true business performance is better viewed on a constant-currency basis, where total revenues would have been up 6% to $211.5 million and EBIT up 21% to $21.6 million. The headwinds were largely attributable to the strengthening Australian dollar, given the majority of revenue is sourced from the US. The company holds approximately $155 million in cash with no debt, which Kavanagh describes as a testament to the strength of the core trough-on business.
quote: I think there's there's two ways to look at the result. Actually one is obviously on the reported numbers which are always very important. But the true performance of the business I think is better viewed through the lens of the constant currency result. Um, obviously we had with the strengthening of the Australian dollar, we, um, you know, did have some headwinds with the majority of revenue coming through from the, the US, but on a constant currency basis. It's a different story. We would have had total revenues up 6% for for the year to 211.5 million. But more importantly, down at the bottom line, the Ebit growth for the year would have been up 21% to 21.6 million. So through the lens of our constant currency, the actual performance of the business was was quite strong.
episode_title: Nanosonics's growth pipeline in a troubled trade environment

headline: Nanosonics expects continued North America installed base expansion and strong upgrade cycle growth, with 32% upgrade growth in FY26
reasoning: Nanosonics has over 34,000 trough-on devices in operation across North America, with the technology now standard of care in the largest ultrasound decontamination market globally. The company brought in a third-generation device and sees around 8,000 older first-generation devices still in the market representing a significant upgrade opportunity. Kavanagh expects continued expansion of the installed base as well as strong ongoing upgrade-driven revenue, having seen 32% upgrade growth in the US in FY26.
quote: North America, I mean, the great thing about it is we've got this. Panasonic's an Australian company that does all its uh, all research and development, all its manufacturing here in Australia. And we've managed to establish a technology called Troll Fund is used in ultrasound decontamination, as is standard of care in the biggest market in the world in North America. There's well over about 34,000 devices in operation. Pretty much every hospital around the United States will be using, um, that technology. But over there we expect the the installed base to continue to expand, um, next year and beyond. There's still plenty of room to grow, but on the upgrade cycle, we did bring in the third generation of the device. And so especially those older first generation devices since about 8000 of those still in the marketplace. Um, we're expecting, you know, strong vitality in the ongoing growth from upgrades to come through.

headline: Nanosonics launching Corus endoscope reprocessing system in UK, Ireland and Australia, with US to follow, as next major growth leg.
reasoning: Nanosonics has spent over eight years developing Corus, an automated cleaning solution for the initial phase of endoscope reprocessing — a complex problem given the small internal lumens of endoscopes. The product has completed controlled market release with positive early feedback and is now entering full commercial launch starting in the UK, Ireland and Australia, with the US to follow. Management expects constant-currency revenue growth of 8–12% for the current financial year, with gross margins of 74–76% despite some tariff-related pressure. Incremental opex will rise due to Corus launch costs, though the core trough-on device business is expected to continue growing revenues and expanding operating margins independently.
quote: So um, from from an outlook perspective, we are on a constant currency basis. We are expecting growth in the order of 8 to 12%. Um, our gross margin in particular because of the tariffs, a bit of moderation on the gross margin, but still relatively high between 74 and 76%. And we're now entering into the launch year of, um, Corus. So as you can imagine, there'll be an incremental increase in opex associated with the launch. And that incremental increase is all, um, associated with chorus. So whereas for the trough on only business, what you're going to see or what we expect to deliver this financial year is ongoing growth. Obviously from a revenue perspective and a profitability, as we continue to expand the operating margins in that business.

headline: Nanosonics warns of 12.5% tariff headwind on capital equipment exports to the US in FY27, but consumables manufacturing shifted to US to partially offset impact
reasoning: Nanosonics faces a 12.5% tariff on capital equipment shipped to the United States in FY27. In FY26, the company was able to recover approximately $2.5 million in tariffs paid up to February, meaning the net tariff impact year-on-year was broadly similar between FY25 and FY26. To partially mitigate ongoing tariff exposure, the company has moved manufacturing of consumables — which represent the majority of revenue — to the United States. Freight cost increases, driven by geopolitical factors and elevated oil prices, represent an additional margin headwind that management hopes will moderate through the new financial year.
quote: In this last year, they certainly impact. And in the last year, um, fortunate, we were able to get the return of the majority of the tariffs that we did pay up to February, about $2.5 million return. So, you know, year on year, the amount that we paid on tariffs in FY 25 and FY 26 was very, very similar. But as we all know now, there's a 12.5% increase or our tariff, uh, coming through uh, this year for the capital equipment that will be shipping to the United States. The one important thing that we have done, uh, on the current tariff side is, uh, the majority of revenue comes through the consumables that actually go through the, um, trough on machine and, and the chorus machine, now that it's launching and we're doing the manufacturing for those consumables in the United States.
episode_title: Nanosonics's growth pipeline in a troubled trade environment
